objections.claim: The no-progress count cannot fire in the main stall cases. Version 3 increments `stalls` only "on a kill with no new checkpoint". But the entry checkpoint means every call that gets going leaves a new checkpoint. And a safe-point stop at exit 5 is not a kill at all. So a run that reaches the same position call after call is never counted, and the loop runs silently forever. That is the case the owner approved `no_progress_calls` for.
objections.evidence: Two paths reach this. (a) A kill after the entry checkpoint. §2.0 step 2 emits a checkpoint "before the re-brief or any other expensive work, so that every call that starts leaves a state behind". The kill branch then has `currentCheckpoint` and returns `other.state = encodeInterview(currentCheckpoint)` (mcp/lyric_tools.js:2901). That is the harness's own checkpoint, carrying the incoming `stalls` unchanged. The `stalls + 1` re-seal in §2.3(d) is never reached. T5's "Three kills during the re-brief yield the no-progress report" therefore cannot pass, because kills during the re-brief come after the entry checkpoint. Q4 motivated the field with exactly this case: the 104-line undeclared re-brief at 1,307 s against a 600 s deadline. That case is a kill after the entry checkpoint, every call. (b) A clean exit-5 stop. §2.3(b) stops when "time left is less than the longest step so far plus the cost of stopping". When the re-brief is longer than half the budget, every call re-briefs, finds too little time left, and stops before the menu at the same cursor. The 60-line undeclared whole grade is 324.8 s (§1.3). Past 91 lines warm does not help (§1.3, PAIR_MEMO_CAP). No kill happens, so nothing counts. Two more gaps: version 3 never says who resets `stalls` when progress resumes, and for `run_id` callers the RUNS record is only re-put inside `if (currentCheckpoint)` (lyric_tools.js:2890-2915), so a re-sealed stall has no revision to ride on.
objections.what_would_resolve: Define the counter by position, not by whether a checkpoint exists. On every non-question result (a kill or exit 5), compare the returned state's position and journal digest with the incoming state's. If neither advanced, carry `stalls + 1`, re-sealed, whichever state is returned (the entry checkpoint or the incoming one). Reset it on any advance. Update RUNS and the run revision with it. Make T5 cover a kill after the entry checkpoint and a repeated exit-5 stop at the same cursor.

objections.claim: A safe-point stop placed "before judging an answer" means the writer's answer never gets a published verdict. The call that sent the answer ends at exit 5 through the `other` branch, which computes no `folded`. The next call has no pending answer in its incoming state, so `foldedOf` returns nothing for it either. Defect 2 comes back on exactly the long-song path this redesign is for.
objections.evidence: `foldedOf` reads only the incoming state's `pending` with a non-empty answer (mcp/lyric_tools.js:433-442: `const pend = prev.pending ... if (pend.answer == null ...) return null`). The `other` branch (lyric_tools.js:2885-2923) sets status, state, final_draft and run_id, but no `folded` or `asked`. The exit-5 state has no pending question, so the following call's `foldedOf(a.state, st)` returns null, even though that call's `verify` writes the outcome. §2.3(b) names "before judging an answer" as the first permitted stop point. On a long song that is the most likely place to stop, since a cold menu-free verify is 574.7 s at 60 lines. §2.2's `waiting` list covers only batch members still unjudged at a suspension. Once judged, an answer leaves that list and is never published. The same holds if the stop comes after the verdict: `other` still publishes none.
objections.what_would_resolve: Have the exit-5 (and kill) result fold against the journal, not only against the incoming `pending`. Carry the answers sent but not yet folded in the state (sealed), with a `waiting` entry ("judged on the next call"). Have whichever call writes their outcome publish them in `folded`. Extend T3 with a stop placed between the answer and its verify.

objections.claim: A fallback replay keeps `accepted_lines` at its furthest value and puts the cursor in its own fields. But the next call resumes from that cursor with `replaying = False`, and its entry checkpoint is written "on the cursor draft". The harness's checkpoint writes `accepted_lines = current`, so `accepted_lines` falls back to the cursor's earlier draft. Every acceptance that call replays on the way to the frontier does the same. A kill then publishes a `final_draft` missing edits the writer already had accepted, which is the B5 failure, one call later.
objections.evidence: lyric_harness.py:8205-8218: `replaying = st["accepted_lines"] != list(lines)`, `if replaying: if list(current) != st["accepted_lines"]: return`, then `trial = dict(st, accepted_lines=list(current), ...)`. §2.0 lists "1. sets replaying = False; 2. emits one checkpoint on the cursor draft" unconditionally. The cursor table itself records the case: "the current draft, as a fingerprint plus a flag when it equals accepted_lines, else in full". The kill branch publishes `exactDraft = ... currentCheckpoint?.accepted_lines` as `final_draft` (lyric_tools.js:2643-2647, 2903). T5 checks `final_draft` only on the killed fallback call, not on the resumed call after it.
objections.what_would_resolve: Set `replaying = False` only when the cursor draft equals `accepted_lines`. Otherwise keep the own-fields checkpoint mode (cursor advances, `accepted_lines` untouched) until the walk reaches the frontier, including for the entry checkpoint. Add a T5 case that kills the second call, resumed from a mid-replay cursor, and asserts `final_draft` equals the furthest `accepted_lines`.

objections.claim: Version 3 routes exit 5 through the existing `other` branch, but that branch publishes only the last stdout checkpoint (`r.checkpoint`), never the state file the verb writes. Version 3 never requires the stop to print a checkpoint carrying the stop position. If it only writes the state file, as exit 4 does, the stop hands back the entry checkpoint or an earlier one, and the work done in that call is lost.
objections.evidence: lyric_tools.js:2629-2636: `currentCheckpoint = r.checkpoint && ...`; :2901: `other.state = encodeInterview(currentCheckpoint)`. Unlike the exit-4 and finish branches (lyric_tools.js:2697, 2832), `other` does not read `statePath`. The CLI's suspension path writes `say_proposer.state` to the state file (lyric_harness.py:13245-13247), and the CLI resumes from that file. So exit 5 needs both a checkpoint (for the connector) and the file (for the CLI). §2.3(b) only says the harness "times its own state write and checkpoint print". The batch-under-construction cursor ("A call that stops between members is continued by the next call") depends on this.
objections.what_would_resolve: State that a safe-point stop always prints a final control checkpoint holding the stop cursor (status e.g. `stopped`), and also writes the state file for the CLI. Have T4 drive the connector, not only the loop, and assert that the returned `state` holds the stop position.

objections.claim: The list of mint points misses one. chat.js's checkpoint recovery mints an interview `state` wire with `encodeState` directly. That state would reach lyric_revise unsealed, fail the seal, and be reported as `cursor_stripped: seal`. A server-minted state would be labelled as tampered, and the chat's recovery path would pay a full replay.
objections.evidence: mcp/chat.js:445-460: `wire = encodeState(cp)` ... `...(decl.writer === 'interview' ? { state: wire } : { checkpoint: wire })` inside `router.recoverCheckpoint` (chat.js:408-480). `grep encodeState mcp/*.js` finds this site beside the ones version 3 lists (lyric_tools.js:2607/2674/2796/2902 and workflow_sessions.js:554). Round 1's B4 ruling required "List every place a state wire is minted and seal each one".
objections.what_would_resolve: Add chat.js `recoverCheckpoint` to the mint points, sealed with the same cursor key imported from lyric_tools.js. Or seal inside one shared encode helper that every interview mint goes through. Add a T7 case that recovers a chat job checkpoint and resumes from its cursor.

objections.claim: One consumer mis-handles exit 5, and version 3's audit list leaves it out: the website chat's `carryState` in gemini_agent.js. An exit-5 interview result has status `interrupted`, a `state` and no `checkpoint`, and every branch of `carryState` falls through it to `return prev`. The chat keeps the previous state, drops the stop's cursor, and the next chat continuation redoes the same work.
objections.evidence: mcp/gemini_agent.js:1151-1154: the interrupted branch requires `typeof verdict.checkpoint === 'string'` (kitchen only). :1167 requires `code === 4`. :1210 requires `code === 3 || status === 'uncertified'`. :1233-1234: `if (code === 0 ...) return null; return prev;`. Interview runs exist on that surface: the code-4 branch carries `verdict[STATE_PROPERTY]`, and chat.js:460 mints interview states. §4.1 lists only lyric_workflow.js, client.js, verdict_view.js and python_bridge.js as "checked for exit-code and field assumptions".
objections.what_would_resolve: Add gemini_agent.js to §4.1. Have `carryState` carry an `interrupted` result's `state` (interview) the way it carries `checkpoint` (kitchen), as resumable. Add a chat-surface test of an exit-5 interview result.

objections.claim: The rebuild rule, "the latest (round, attempt) per line or member tuple, dropped if accepted", is not the rule the hooks apply, in two places. (1) The group hook keeps the last write in walk order, and two group questions on the same member tuple can share a round and an attempt. (2) Version 3 never says how the new `not_applied` record (`accepted: null`) affects the rebuild or the live hooks.
objections.evidence: (1) `record_group` overwrites `last_grej[_m]` on every call (lyric_harness.py:8135-8139), keyed only on the member tuple. `members` is the mandate's own order, whatever the pivot (`_brief_key`, lyric_harness.py:7386-7411). `_try_tier2` starts `attempt` at 0 for each pivot (loop.py:1567-1580). So pivot L1 and pivot L2 escalating the same couplet in one round give two entries with equal (members, round, attempt) and different `question_sha256`. "Latest (round, attempt)" ties, and a `max` picks the first, while the hook keeps the second. The next round's `_prior_group` text and `question_sha256` then differ from a full replay, and the recorded answer misses. (2) `record` does `bool(accepted)` and sets `last_rej` on anything not accepted (lyric_harness.py:7925-7948). `_attempt_block` renders a prior as "Your line ... in ROUND r was REJECTED ... The grader's reasons, verbatim" (propose.py:485-496). So a `not_applied` entry that reaches either path tells the writer something false. If the live path skips it and the rebuild does not (or the reverse), cursor and replay produce different question bytes.
objections.what_would_resolve: State the rule as "the last entry in list order per line / member tuple, among `accepted` true/false entries only, popped on `accepted: true`". State that `not_applied` records are written without calling `record` and are skipped by the rebuild. Add a T1 script with two same-round escalations of one couplet, and one with a `not_applied` line asked again in a later round.

objections.claim: The cursor table leaves out the in-progress round's `attempts` list, the LineAttempt records that become `RoundResult.attempts` when the round closes. Only finished rounds are stored by reference. Some of these attempts have no outcome record to refer to: tier-2 attempts that were never asked (pinned, starved) and escalation labels. A resume that enters mid-pass cannot produce the same `LoopResult.rounds`, which T1 compares.
objections.evidence: loop.py:1989 `attempts, fixed_this_round, touched = [], [], set()`. Appended at :2185, :2261 and :2271. Closed at :2277 `rounds.append(RoundResult(round_no, attempts, ...))`. The reasons are built from control flow and menus: "after tier 1 found no accepted line, escalated to tier 2: ..." (:2266-2270), "after tier 2 {NOT ASKED|unaccepted}, fell through ..." (:2188-2194), and `_try_tier2`'s unasked refusals, which carry `pinned`/`starved` counts from anchor menu searches. None of these is in `outcomes`. The cursor table lists `touched`, `fixed_this_round`, `resolved_elsewhere` and "the finished rounds", not the current round's attempts. The same applies to the whole-draft repair's `_attempts` (:1952-1953).
objections.what_would_resolve: Add the current round's attempts, and the global phase's `_attempts`, to the cursor: by reference where an outcome exists, verbatim otherwise. Add a T1 assertion on `LoopResult.rounds` for a suspension mid-pass after an unasked tier-2 attempt.

objections.claim: "Materialized menu inputs (the offered and forbidden lists the question was rendered with)" is far less than the rendered question and the control flow read. A cursor holding only those two lists cannot reproduce question bytes or the group-first and batch-skip decisions without rebuilding the menu. A cursor holding everything the renderer reads is much larger than version 3 assumes.
objections.evidence: The offers block sets about a dozen more fields (revise.py:6143-6217): `fields_by_slot` (per-place SlotField with dropped, by_call, schema_refused, grader_refused, widened, joint_conflict), `screened_out`, `field_computed`, `empty_head_cause`, `joint_conflict`, `partial_by_call`, `schema_refused`, `grader_refused`, `field_widened`, `offer_emptied_by_ban`, `forbidden_incumbent`. The line prompt reads them (propose.py:354-361, 719, 734, 749, 766, 794-803, 810, 889). Control flow reads `field_computed`, `candidates` and `joint_conflict` (`_asks_group_first`, loop.py:2104-2107) and `x.joint_conflict` (prefetch, lyric_harness.py:8060-8061).
objections.what_would_resolve: List exactly which Brief/SlotField fields the cursor stores per materialized question: at least every field the renderers and `_asks_group_first`/prefetch read. Include their bytes in §4.3 item 1's measurement. T1/T4 must compare the prompts of questions rebuilt from the cursor byte for byte.

objections.claim: Cursor bytes are admitted against the worker journal's own capacity. A checkpoint that does not fit raises `_JournalCapacity`, which ends the run for good. Two new checkpoints can do this where today's code would carry on: a mid-construction checkpoint holding the partial batch's menus, and a fallback-replay checkpoint holding the cursor draft in full. The first happens outside prefetch's `try`, so the batch is not trimmed but the run ends. That breaks "the same journal-capacity trimming".
objections.evidence: `checkpoint` admits `trial` at `ceiling=JOURNAL_BYTES` (lyric_harness.py:8218). `_journal_admit` raises `_JournalCapacity` (:7610-7613), and the verb turns that into `_journal_stop`, which is non-resumable (`new_run_required`, lyric_tools.js:2648-2690). prefetch catches `_JournalCapacity` only around `_suspend` (lyric_harness.py:8081-8090, `except _JournalCapacity: chosen.pop()`). assertContinuationCapacity counts everything except `connector_*` against WORKER_STATE_BYTES (state_codec.js:58-64). A pre-change state that fit without a cursor can fail on its first fallback checkpoint. §2.1 says the cursor is "stored by reference", but menus and a full cursor draft are not references.
objections.what_would_resolve: Either budget the cursor outside the journal's capacity (bounded separately, as `connector_declarations` is), or state that a cursor that does not fit is dropped (`cursor_stripped`) rather than ending the run. Add the partial-batch and fallback-checkpoint cases to §4.3 item 1 and a test that a near-capacity state still resumes.

objections.claim: `journal_digest` is undefined, and version 3 uses it for two things that cannot both hold. As a resume check ("the journal digest mismatches" means fall back), it must stay equal across a call that folds a new answer into `answered`. As the progress measure ("the journal digest advanced: a new question was asked or a new verdict recorded"), it must change when `pending` or `outcomes` change. Read literally, "over the whole journal" makes every answered continuation fall back.
objections.evidence: The harness folds `pending.answer` into the journal at load, before the loop (lyric_harness.py:7735-7790, `folded_base = dict(st, pending=None)`). So the journal a cursor sees at resume always has one more answer than the journal it was minted over. `record`/`record_group` overwrite outcomes in place by key (lyric_harness.py:7930-7942, 8124-8134), so the outcomes list is not append-only. A new question changes `pending`, not `answered`.
objections.what_would_resolve: Define the digest exactly: which fields (answered, outcomes, group_outcomes, pending?), and that the resume check is "the journal the cursor was minted over is an unchanged prefix of the incoming one", not equality. Give the progress measure its own definition (position and verdict count). Add T7 cases: an edited earlier answer falls back, a newly folded answer does not.

objections.claim: The cursor carries "the running stale count". But the proposer disclosure that T1 must match prints the hit count and each stale key, and its header claims a replay that no longer happens. The session's continue text also still says the session "replays its journal".
objections.evidence: `disclosure(done=True)` prints `{tally['hit']} consulted and answered` and lists every stale `(line, attempt, round)` (lyric_harness.py:8191-8199). `tally['hit']` counts lookups this process made (:7980, :8102), so a cursor resume reports a smaller number than a full replay. The header says "answer(s) already given, replayed in order" (:8159). workflow_sessions.js SESSION_RESUME: "the session carries this run and replays its journal" (:93-94). That is published text the Q6 ruling did not cover.
objections.what_would_resolve: Carry `tally.hit` and the full stale key list in the cursor, not a count. Reword the disclosure header and SESSION_RESUME under the Q6 change, and list them in §3.

objections.claim: "A kill that produced no new checkpoint leaves the session's previous sealed continuation in place" is false when the interruption is a server restart. An interrupted operation with no progress record cannot resume, and the session layer then sets the continuation to null.
objections.evidence: workflow_sessions.js:377-386: for `parent.state === 'interrupted'` that is not `resumable`, `session = clone(original); session.native.continuation = null;`. `resumable` fails when `record.progress` is missing (resumeSnapshot, :530-551). The window is narrower now (startup until the entry checkpoint), but T5's B3 case only simulates a bridge kill, which leaves the operation `completed`.
objections.what_would_resolve: Either keep the prior continuation for an interrupted lyric_revise with no progress, or scope 2.3(c)'s claim to bridge kills. Add the restart case to T5.

objections.claim: Session callers will not see the two new result fields on a finished run. The short view keeps a fixed list of fields that holds neither `cursor_stripped` nor `no_progress_calls`. The exit-4 receipt is built by hand from an explicit field list, so the fields must be added there too.
objections.evidence: verdict_view.js:33-51 `KEPT` lists the fields of a finished grade/revise short verdict: no `cursor_stripped`, no `no_progress_calls`. The exit-4 JSON block is assembled field by field (lyric_tools.js:2741-2780). Q5's own reason is that "a caller cannot tell a slow fallback replay from the fast path".
objections.what_would_resolve: Add both fields to `KEPT` and to the hand-built exit-4 receipt. Pin them in the session-view tests.

objections.claim: The one menu §2.4 says it adds, the non-pivot member's one-move menu "computed by tier 1's own call (brief(target_lines={member}), declared_offer)", does not exist in the couplet case it claims to fix. So T6's couplet case cannot pass as specified.
objections.evidence: A pair violation is filed only on the LATER endpoint: revise.py:3712 `add(j, Finding("SCHEME_VIOLATION", ...))`. `brief` builds a Brief only for lines that have per-line findings: revise.py:5811-5813 `for ln in sorted(found["per_line"]): if targets is not None and ln not in targets: continue`. On escalation the pivot is the flagged line (loop.py:2262, `_try_tier2(reviser, b, ...)` with b = L2), so the non-pivot member is the earlier endpoint. Measured read-only on a 2-line non-rhyming couplet ('I set the kettle on the stove' / 'and waited for the morning light') with mandate [[1,2]]: per_line keys [2]; `brief(lines, m, target_lines={1})` returns []. The design's own fallback ("no single-line finding on L1; no one-move menu was computed") is what would print, not L1's words. §2.4 already concedes the no-Brief case, so the claimed gain contradicts the design's own text.
objections.what_would_resolve: Compute the non-pivot member's one-move menu from the mandate rather than from a Brief: the calls of the groups bound at the member's own place (`_slot_of`), then `joint_field_screened`, then `declared_offer` at that slot, exactly as brief() does for a line that has one. State this in §2.4, and make T6's couplet fixture one where L1 carries no per-line finding. Otherwise, say plainly that defect 4 stays open for couplets.

objections.claim: Option B's four verdicts do not cover every way today's walk discards a batch answer. Two skip paths are not `resolved_elsewhere`. On those paths v3 lists the dead answer as `pending` forever: a false statement while the run lives, and `unknown` once it stops.
objections.evidence: Line answers are keyed (line, attempt, round) (lyric_harness.py:7414-7436), so an answer not consumed in its own round is never consumed. Path 1: loop.py:2011 `if b.line_no in touched: continue` is a silent skip, with no resolved_elsewhere entry. Path 2: when the walk reaches a member, `_asks_group_first(b)` is re-evaluated on the moved draft (loop.py:2137, 2173). If that group is accepted, `_try_tier1` is never called and the batch's attempt-0 answer is never read. Both are reachable. prefetch drops a group-first or already-answered ahead line with `continue` and does NOT add its related set to `rels` (lyric_harness.py:8048-8049, 8058-8062). So a later member related to that skipped line can be chosen, and the skipped line's group rewrite then touches the member. v3 defines `waiting` as "Every batch answer on record with no outcome" and `not_applied` only for resolved_elsewhere. Separately, `not_applied`'s `why` ("naming the line whose acceptance closed it") is not computable from today's walk. At loop.py:2097 the closure happened at an earlier re-brief, and nothing records which acceptance caused it. At loop.py:2130 (`_materialize` returned None) there may be no acceptance at all.
objections.what_would_resolve: Give the touched skip and the group-accepted-before-tier-1 case a recorded standing too, as `not_applied` with why 'superseded by the accepted rewrite of L..'. Scope `waiting` to answers of the current round that the walk has not yet passed, which needs a loop-to-proposer hook carrying the walk position. Track the acceptance that preceded the re-brief at which a line disappeared, and give the :2130 path its own why. T3 should add a fixture for each path.

objections.claim: The new `not_applied` outcome row collides with the rejection history (`last_rej`) and with the coupling test. The design leaves its write path unspecified, and every available choice breaks something it promises.
objections.evidence: record() hard-codes `"accepted": bool(accepted)` (lyric_harness.py:7928) and sets `last_rej[line]` for any non-accepted entry (:7943-7948). `_prior` renders that entry into the next round's line question (:7965-7975, :8007). Case 1, the row is written through `record`: an answer that was never judged is shown to the writer next round as a rejection, with reasons=[why], and line-question bytes change from today's. Case 2, it is written another way: §2.0's re-derivation rule for `last_rej` ("the latest (round, attempt) per line, dropped if accepted") treats the accepted:null row as latest and not accepted, so a cursor resume rebuilds a `last_rej` that a full replay never had, and T1 fails. loop.py, where §4.1 puts the write, does not hold the proposer's `ones`, so it cannot tell which skipped lines have an answer on record. The coupling test requires "the run's outcomes ... equal those of today's code on the same journal". Its own scenario (two independent members sharing ANAPHORA_OVERLOAD) is the one where member 1's acceptance closes member 2's finding, which sends member 2 through resolved_elsewhere and adds a `not_applied` row. Today's code has no such row, so the test fails on the new code.
objections.what_would_resolve: Specify a separate hook, e.g. `propose.skipped(line, round, why)`, that writes the row only when the proposer holds an answer for that key. Exclude disposition rows from `last_rej`, both when it is maintained live and in the §2.0 rebuild, and add a T1 script that crosses a `not_applied` row. Restate the coupling test as equality of the judged outcomes (accepted true/false) and the final draft, with `not_applied` rows compared separately.

objections.claim: "Why pending is not stored" is false as designed. The `waiting` list rides on the pending record, and the code copies that record into `answered` and charges it against the journal ceiling. That can change batch membership and stop runs earlier, which contradicts "the walk order ... stays exactly as today" and "Cost: nothing measurable".
objections.evidence: Folding an answer copies the whole pending record into the replay file: lyric_harness.py:7779 `rec, ans = dict(pend["record"]), pend["answer"]`, then :7836-7838 `st["answered"]["propose"].append(rec)` for single questions and :7856-7857 `st["answered"]["propose_group"].append(rec)` for group questions. So every answered question permanently carries its `waiting` list. `_suspend` admits the whole pending record, `trial = dict(st, pending=pending)` (:7959-7961). A failed admission inside prefetch trims the batch (:8089-8090 `except _JournalCapacity: chosen.pop()`), which yields a different batch and different question bytes from today's on the same journal. On a single or group suspension the failure propagates to the journal_capacity branch, a stop that today's code would not reach. §4.3 item 1 measures state bytes without these lists.
objections.what_would_resolve: Carry `waiting` outside `pending.record`, for example as its own top-level result or state field that is never folded into `answered` and is excluded from the reserve `_suspend` charges. Alternatively, strip it at fold time and say so. Include it in §4.3's state-byte measurement, and add a test that a run near JOURNAL_WORK_BYTES chooses the same batch members as today.

objections.claim: A `pending` answer's eventual verdict is never published. And on the new exit-5 path, a batch answered in that call gets no verdict at all, which is defect 2 reintroduced by a path this design creates.
objections.evidence: foldedOf folds only the PREVIOUS pending question's own rows (lyric_tools.js:433-466: `askedOf(pend)`; batch rows come from `pend.record.records`). In T3's next call, prev.pending is the L1+L2 group question, so foldedOf returns that question's verdict only. L4, judged later in that same walk, never appears in any `folded`. The exit-5 stop is routed through the generic interrupted branch (lyric_tools.js:2885-2923), which sets no `folded` field. It is the only branch with none (compare :2753 and :2839). A safe-point stop also has no pending question, so there is no `pending.record.waiting` to render `pending` from. foldedOne's own `unknown`/`unverified` default (:409-430) is what remains for any consumer that later tries.
objections.what_would_resolve: (1) foldedOf also folds the previous pending's `waiting` entries against the new state's outcomes, using only the four owner-approved values. (2) The exit-5 branch carries `folded` for the answer it consumed, with `waiting` computed at the safe point. Define in which state's pending foldedOne looks for `waiting`: the new one. (3) T3 continues one more call and asserts L4's final verdict. Add an exit-5 case in which a batch is folded and the call stops before the next question.

objections.claim: As specified, the no-progress count cannot fire in the case the owner approved it for, and T5's "three kills during the re-brief" case cannot pass.
objections.evidence: §2.0 step 2 emits a checkpoint "before the re-brief or any other expensive work, so that every call that starts leaves a state behind". §2.3(d) increments the stall count only "On a kill with no new checkpoint". So a kill during the re-brief always has a new checkpoint (the entry one), the kill branch publishes it (lyric_tools.js:2894-2900 `other.state = encodeInterview(currentCheckpoint)`), and the count never moves. An exit-5 stop that makes no progress (the re-brief consumed the budget and the next menu cannot start) is not a kill, so it is never counted either. That leaves Q4's own case, a 104-line song whose cold grade is 1,307 s against a 600 s deadline, looping silently. The contradiction is inherited from judge 1's two B8 requirements, combined literally.
objections.what_would_resolve: Define the trigger by the definition of progress in §2.3(d)'s first bullet, not by whether a checkpoint exists. The connector compares the newest checkpoint's (journal digest, cursor phase/position) with the incoming state's, and re-seals with stalls+1 whenever neither advanced, on a kill and on exit 5 alike. defense.design_change: Rewrite §2.3(d). The connector defines a call's position as (cursor phase/index, round, members done in any batch or group question under construction, the count of verdict and disposition records, and the identity of the pending question). On every result that asks no new question (a kill, exit 5, interrupted or other), it compares the returned state's position with the incoming state's. If nothing advanced, it carries `stalls + 1` into whichever state it returns, the entry checkpoint or the incoming state, and re-seals it. Any advance, and any exit-4 result that asks a new question, resets it to 0. The re-sealed state is always put into RUNS with a new revision, including when no checkpoint was printed, and the session layer stores it. At 2 or more the result carries `no_progress_calls`, and no call is ever refused. T5 adds three cases: three kills after the entry checkpoint, during the re-brief, must give `no_progress_calls >= 2`; three exit-5 stops at the same cursor must give the same; and a call that advances must reset the count to 0.
